messages:
ian: heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak rolled at 08:10 we see p95 latency for short sequences (<=32 tokens) jump ~1.6x on a few clusters. Not universal but reproducible in prod-canary.
morgan: ugh. which tweak? the FP16 kernel path change? :grimacing:
deploy-bot: rollout v3.18.2 -> runtime-group-a completed (canary 10%); no automatic rollback triggered.
dina: I pulled traces — short requests are getting pushed onto the ‘long-path’ kernel due to our sequence-length-hinting heuristic. That increases per-token overhead and prevents them from getting coalesced into microbatches.
leo: timeline: was the kernel hint decision moved to after admit? if so we might be batching wrong.
ian: yes, we moved kernel decision later so it picks kernels after KV-lookup info. intention was better kernel k-selection for long cache hits, but side-effect is short-seq admit into mixed batches
morgan: mixed batches are killing cache locality + forcing a slower kernel. perf-bot: sample profile: CPU sys-time up 30%, GPU kernel-launch latency up 9ms median for short requests.
dina: proposal: add a lightweight early-path kernel hint that classifies "very short" requests (<48 tokens) before admit and pins them to short-fast kernel and a dedicated microbatch queue. That avoids mixing with long ones.
leo: +1. Also we should consider token_budget_target per-tenant so greedy tenants with long sequences don't starve short interactive tenants. Currently global target lets long jobs consume most credits during high load.
ian: agreed. experiment plan: 1) early kernel hint + dedicate slot queue for short path; 2) token_budget_target enforcement (soft reclaim after 200ms); 3) KV priming tweak — prefetch common prefixes for short requests to keep KV hit-rate high.
morgan: can we simulate this in canary? I can wire a config toggle: 
```json
{
  "short_path_token_limit": 48,
  "short_queue_capacity": 64,
  "token_budget_target_ms": 200,
  "early_kernel_hint_enabled": true
}
```
leo: add per-tenant override so we can test with a noisy-tenant pair.
perf-bot: added loadtest scenario: interactive-short + streaming-long overlay. baseline run attached to thread (summary: short p95 -> 225ms, proposed -> 110ms; long throughput -2.5%).
dina: acceptable tradeoff if long only drops slightly, but we must avoid regression to tail for long. Suggest kernel time-slicing: allow preemption of long microbatches if short queue non-empty and short p99 > threshold.
ian: careful with preemption — introduces KV state churn. preempting cold long batches could regress long more. We'll only preempt if KV hit rate for long batch > 50% (so it won't require heavy priming on resume).
morgan: notes for rollout: feature flags gated by tenant list, telemetry hooks: per-queue latency, kv-hit-rate, kernel-choice, token-credit-snapshots. default off for existing clusters.
leo: I'll add a small e2e canary on prod-canary-3 with two tenants: internal-chat (short) + analytics (long). target two-hour run.
dina: thanks — I'll monitor and collect flamegraphs. If short p95 improves and long drop <=5%, we promote.
ian: for RFC docs, I'll draft a short design with diagrams and config knobs. tagging @morgan @leo for review by EOD. :thumbsup:
morgan: cool, ping me when draft's up. I'll prepare canary toggle.
perf-bot: note: alert rule created: runtime.short-path.p95 > 300ms for 5m => pager for eng-runtime-oncall.
leo: typo in config above — short_queue_capacity should be 256, not 64. updating canary PR.
ian: final: let's keep rollout conservative. thanks all.
